claims.text: The as-cast Nb35Zr26Ti19Hf15Mo5 alloy is produced by vacuum levitation melting.
The as-cast alloy is a single-phase BCC solid solution.
The as-cast alloy has approximately 100 micrometer equiaxed grains.
The as-cast alloy exhibits weak dendritic/interdendritic elemental segregation.
Cold rolling to 80% reduction followed by annealing for 20 minutes at 750 °C will improve the alloy's strength-plasticity balance.
Cold rolling elongates and preferentially orients the grains.
Cold rolling increases dislocation accumulation.
Cold rolling increases the fraction of low- and medium-angle boundaries.
Cold rolling develops a strong <101>(111) texture.
Annealing at 750 °C promotes partial recovery.
Annealing at 750 °C produces necklace-like partial recrystallization.
The anneal reduces dislocation density to a moderate level while retaining beneficial work hardening.
Work hardening from rolling-induced dislocations and texture increases strength while reducing ductility.
Controlled recovery and partial recrystallization reduce barriers to slip, increasing plasticity without fully eliminating rolling-derived strength.
The as-cast alloy has a tensile strength of approximately 1007 MPa and elongation of approximately 23%.
The unannealed 80%-rolled alloy has a tensile strength of approximately 1408 MPa and elongation of approximately 10.5%.
Annealing the 80%-rolled alloy at 750 °C for 20 minutes will reduce tensile strength by approximately 10-15% relative to the unannealed rolled state.
Annealing the 80%-rolled alloy at 750 °C for 20 minutes will increase elongation from approximately 10.5% toward or above 20%.
The predicted trend applies to cold-rolling reductions from 20% to 80% and annealing temperatures from 650 °C to 800 °C.
The predicted strength-plasticity improvement applies under room-temperature tensile testing at 1 mm/min.
